controls.answer:
According to the documentation: If allow_nan is false (default: True), then it will be a ValueError to serialize out of range float values (nan, inf, -inf) in strict compliance of the JSON specification. If allow_nan is true, their JavaScript equivalents (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity) will be used.

Source excerpt: allow_nan_false_valueerror: True; ensure_ascii_default_true: True; ensure_ascii_escapes_non_ascii: True; jsondecodeerror_invalid_document: True; loads_bytes_bytearray: True; read_text_signature: encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None; sort_keys_sorts_dicts: True
Passing allow_nan=False makes the encoder raise a ValueError when it meets NaN or an infinity, rather than writing NaN or Infinity tokens that strict JSON does not allow.
allow_nan=false emits NaN as the JavaScript token, so nothing is raised.
With allow_nan=False the encoder silently replaces NaN and the infinities with null.
